beta_new: Starts with a 5.8 crack that transitions left through a bolted section holding the initial crux. A knee-bar rest sits below a roof; pull through onto face climbing, then a balancy sequence to an amazing finger rail, finishing with a wild romp on the left side.

Grade II, 5.8, fully bolted. Start at the first two bolts on a short prow at the lowest toe of the West Face. P1 climbs a short face to clean ramps to a ledge belay; P2 traverses a saddle to a chain anchor; P3 is bolted with a semi-hanging belay on a small ledge and significant exposure; P4 climbs an arete/basalt band to the summit. Pitches 3-4 are commonly combined with alpine draws.

Most parties approach via the historic Monte Cristo townsite and the Glacier Basin Trail, then leave the maintained trail to work up talus/scree toward the col on the dividing ridge below the Wilmans Spires before gaining the northwest ridge for the final Class 4 scramble to the summit. This northwest ridge line is the peak's easiest route.

From the trailhead between the two Twin Lakes, the trail climbs moderately steeply through blueberry and heather slopes, meeting the High Pass Trail (#676) junction at about a quarter to half mile (stay left/straight for Winchester). It continues in tight switchbacks through fireweed and blueberries, crests a saddle/pass near 1.3 miles, then follows the final ridge to the restored 1935 lookout at the 6,521-ft summit. A short rock-cut section near the top is exposed and requires care, especially with children or dogs.

A third option to reach Windy Peak, starting near Hodges Horse Pasture at the Iron Gate Trailhead. The line follows the Boundary Trail (#533) north to Sunny Pass, then turns west to join the Windy Peak Trail for the final approach and the same Class 2 summit scramble used by the other two routes. It involves more ascent/descent along the way than the Long Swamp or Windy Creek approaches for a similar or shorter map distance.

From Long Swamp Campground, Trail #342 climbs steadily through burned lodgepole pine to the Pasayten Wilderness boundary (~2.5 mi in), then continues through open, recovering burn and meadow to 'Two Bear Camp' (water available) and on to the Windy Peak area before the maintained tread tops out just below the true summit. The final roughly 200-300 vertical feet to the actual high point leaves the constructed trail for an easy, well-cairned Class 2 scramble over open talus/rock — the only 'technical' part of an otherwise non-technical alpine hike. Past the summit the trail continues down to join the Boundary Trail at Horseshoe Basin, so parties doing an out-and-back to just the peak should watch their turn point.

This alternate ('Windy Peak via the Windy Creek Trail') cuts distance versus the Long Swamp approach by starting further west/higher along Toats Coulee Road. The Windy Creek Trail climbs to meet the upper Windy Peak trail network, then shares the same final easy scramble to the true summit. The trail is clear near the first creek crossing but has accumulated blowdown further along, so expect some deadfall to step over/around in less-maintained years.

Wing Peak has no maintained trail. Parties approach via the Barclay Creek/Tailgunner Creek drainage to Tailgunner Pass, then climb steep snow faces and rock benches along the peak's northwest ridge. The crux is a roughly 70-degree, heavily exposed snowfinger just below the summit, above which loose Class 4 rock leads to the top. Most parties climb Wing as part of a 2-3 day traverse with Gunn Peak and Tailgunner Peak, camping near Tailgunner Pass.

Begins on the line of the summer East Face for roughly two pitches, then traverses left about 30 ft with limited protection into a corner below a steep rock barrier. The crux pitch climbs this corner at about 5.8-ish with one short aid move (A0) or M5 mixed climbing to a tree belay, after which a final pitch of steep snow (using small trees for anchors) trends slightly right to finish near the summit. accounts describe the line in these general sections rather than a strict pitch-by-pitch account across all 5 rope-lengths. Rated Grade III, PG13, reflecting sustained runout climbing on marginal protection.

This route approaches from the south after descending Aasgard Pass into the Upper Enchantments. Navigate south and southwest toward the tower's base, ascending toward the white granitic wall. Find a ledge to traverse around the east side of the tower, then scramble large black granite blocks to reach the summit. A 4-foot slot requires a jump to access the true summit. The route is exposed and requires careful footwork, especially on descent.

From the col just southwest of the tower, ascend the sharp ridge about 100 ft, traverse a few feet right onto the South Face (Class 4), make a step-up 5.5 move, climb a short face, and scramble to the summit, jumping a 4-ft slot to reach the true top. Protection placements on the crux can be tricky to find, so an experienced leader is recommended.
The route climbs mostly Class 4 rock with a short Class 5 chimney partway up, on solid granite with good natural hand- and footholds, finishing with a friction-face section to the summit.

moves.from: From the col/notch behind the tower, cross a steep snowfield (ice axe recommended) to reach the base.

beta_new: One of the most popular routes at Keechelus and possibly the best 5.10 here. Features easy initial bolts followed by sustained jug hauling with a spectacular position.

From the Tungsten Mine Camp junction (where Tungsten Creek Trail #534 meets Boundary Trail #533, at ~6,750 ft on the mountain's south side), follow the Boundary Trail roughly a mile west/northwest to where it bends south, then leave the trail and ascend cross-country, angling northeast up the gentle west-facing slope to the summit. Done on this line the off-trail portion is YDS Class 2; other lines/variations on the mountain may require short, low-level Class 3 scrambling. The west-slope line is reported to be the safest, least steep, and most commonly recommended way to the top.
Follows the obvious long fingercrack layback corner on a buttress near Ellation. Often combined with Blood Orgy (rappel or downclimb between the two).

4-pitch trad climbing route graded 5.11a/b (also 6c/23/VIII-/E3 in other systems). Granite climbing on Cutthroat Creek Wall. Expect lichen and loose rock (first climbed in 2009 and seldom repeated). Early season may have snow/ice hazards. Rock is granite of good quality.

moves.from: From parking, hike approximately 1/4 mile on old roadbed, look for cairns marking left turn uphill. Bushwhack through woods with no trail, gaining elevation quickly. Traverse leftward in open forest and on slabby benches to reach shoulder at base of wall's right-hand side.
moves.value: From the parking area, hike about a quarter mile on an old roadbed and watch for cairns marking a left turn uphill. Bushwhack through the woods with no trail, gaining elevation quickly, then traverse leftward through open forest and slabby benches to the shoulder at the base of the wall's right-hand side.

moves.from: Trad protection: doubles to a #3 Camalot, weighted toward small cams and wires, with RPs for thin seams.

rows.sizes: doubles to #3 Camalot, weighted toward small sizes

value.text: Cams in doubles to a #3 Camalot, weighted toward small sizes, plus wires and RPs for thin seams.

beta_new: Follows the obvious scrub line traversing left under a small roof. Pull the roof on a good crimp, step right, and walk up the slab. Belay at a large dead tree just before the hiking trail. The climbing itself is 'crappy' but it offers a way up to the upper tier with less bushwhacking than the standard walk-off.

Zool Patch starts up double cracks just left of Clean Break, climbs a 5.9 offwidth flake on pitch 2, then trends left on a brushy, poorly protected traverse across blank slabs (avoided rather than climbed directly) to a pair of bail trees.

moves.from: , from which two double-rope rappels return to the base

beta_new: Right of the big left-facing corner, work up a flake system to a stance, then carry on up the striped wall, clipping one bolt, to cold shuts below the huge roof.

Begin on jugs and follow the bolts as they slant leftward to the anchors. The direct start begins beneath a big crack inside the cave's right side, climbs buckets up and right, then powers past two bolts to merge with the regular route.
Follow the bolted fracture until it ends, roughly thirty feet up, then shift right for a handful of moves and complete the route on the steep wall above, ending at the anchors.
Climb the sharp arete directly, clipping five bolts to reach the anchors.
Use a stick-clip for bolt one, then muscle and leap up the leaning white wall. The two neighbors end at the same lower-off and can be led or toproped for extra pump.
Start below the overlap's right end, then ascend the wall and a dihedral that faces right, reaching the toprope anchors.
Climb the dihedral, then step around the low ceiling's right side to bolt number one. Then a mix of different moves leads straight up the bulging upper section.
Meander up the smooth surface right of the arete, clipping one bolt, then a pin, then two more bolts.

moves.from: A few nuts and small cams add security.

value.text: A few nuts and small cams.

beta_new: Pull on the excellent holds the whole way up the corridor wall's left half to the anchors.
Climb to and along the shallow right-facing dihedral, then drift left to the top anchors of Alien Autopsy.
Take the left-hand bolt line up the slabby wall.
Start in a shallow dihedral facing left under the flaky roof; haul over the low ceiling, then go directly up the wall past a second bulge to the anchors.
Start beneath some small, stacked overhangs and trace the ten bolts straight to the anchors.
Step off a twelve-foot block, angle right past one bolt to a comfortable ledge, then run the crack until it dies and lower off.
Follow Smore Energy through bolt three, then cut left, passing one more bolt, to complete the climb on the arete's top half.

The first pitch works a corner toward a chockstone wedged in the primary flake, then the giant flake and chimney lead to their top, and you shift right to cold shuts.

The next pitch exits the ledge's right edge, trends right over a bulge onto good holds, and traverses about twenty feet to the anchors under Orangeaid and Alcoa Presents.

Start at two shallow corners facing right, below a chockstone flake. Tricky moves gain the corners, then a widening, easier crack goes to a ledge with anchors. A brief corner and a ramp slanting right come next, then work your way back across to the left, onto the ledge under Orangeaid.
Begin as Bourbon Sauce does, but at its roof head right and crank to the Kaos anchors. Then shift back to the left and complete the upper wall to the high lower-off.
Climb poor rock past one bolt, then blast out through the stacked roofs; once you reach bolt five, veer left over a couple more bolts to join the closing section of Mojo Hand.
Start roughly ten feet to the left of the big tree, then work through a face section, a corner and a high roof to the anchors.
Begin where a crack splits a low roof, fifteen feet over from an arete, then tackle the steep face, clipping nine bolts plus a pin.
Step off a minuscule ledge, around three feet high, and head up and to the left, clipping the two bolts.
